re_line: Perdue's arms-offer disclosure · $60B tariff lists · Senators press on Taiwan arms · PBOC stimulus · Xi's National Day Taiwan line
editors_note:
This is the first China Room Brief. Each Tuesday it collects what moved in US-China relations over the past seven days, what is scheduled for the next seven, and what CSIS scholars have in the pipeline.

Washington spent the week after Xi Jinping's state visit working out what the summit produced. The answer so far: two published tariff lists worth $60 billion, an ambassador's disclosure the White House then denied, and senators from both parties pressing for a $14 billion Taiwan arms package that has not moved.

week_at_a_glance.headline: Does Beijing restart fuel exports after Golden Week?
week_at_a_glance.body: Chinese refiners suspended October fuel exports beyond Hong Kong and Macau, and PetroChina cancelled cargoes on Sep 30. Lianhe Zaobao reports it is unclear whether Beijing resumes export approvals when the holiday ends Oct 7. Reuters expects the suspension to tighten diesel and jet fuel across Asia.

week_at_a_glance.headline: Trade terms move on Washington's clock
week_at_a_glance.body: USTR Jamieson Greer said no date is set for tariff cuts under the Board of Trade mechanism, and told Nikkei the US will unveil countermeasures against overproduction from China, Japan and others "within weeks." Reuters reported the US has slowed aircraft-part exports to China to build leverage.

week_at_a_glance.headline: IMF and World Bank open their Annual Meetings in Bangkok
week_at_a_glance.body: China's numbers arrive with fresh support behind them: a nationwide mortgage-interest subsidy took effect Oct 1, and the PBOC's 1.2 trillion yuan reverse repo is set for Oct 8. September manufacturing PMIs came in at 50.1, the first expansion after two months of contraction.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Twenty-one Democrats and four Republicans press for Taiwan arms
heard_on_the_hill.body: Twenty-one Democratic senators led by Jeanne Shaheen urged Trump to "immediately deliver congressionally approved defense assistance to Taiwan," citing $1.3 billion in appropriated funds and a $14 billion package approved nine months ago. Four Republican senators separately called for the assistance to be released.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Wicker: commitments to Taiwan must be upheld
heard_on_the_hill.body: Chairman Roger Wicker said so after meeting Taiwan's representative in Washington, Alexander Yui.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Speaker Johnson rejects the arms-for-trade reading
heard_on_the_hill.body: Mike Johnson said Taiwan's stability matters to US security and the economy, dismissed suggestions that the delayed package is leverage in trade talks, and said Trump will have completed roughly $40 billion in Taiwan arms sales across his two terms.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Chinese car ban pushed past the midterms
heard_on_the_hill.body: The Senate put off a bill that would permanently bar Chinese-made cars until after the Nov 3 elections, AP reported; Reuters says senators plan a vote in November. Sen. Bernie Moreno said his separate bill, covering automakers with more than 15% Chinese ownership, would not touch Mercedes-Benz.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Bipartisan bill targets Chinese optical modules
heard_on_the_hill.body: A bipartisan group of senators proposed barring Chinese-made optical modules from federal national-security systems, with a five-year grace period. Shenzhen's ChiNext index fell 4.53% the next trading day.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Starbucks told to close its first Xinjiang stores
heard_on_the_hill.body: A US congressman demanded the closures, citing forced labor in the region, Reuters reported.

lead.kicker: Most-covered US-China story of the week · 5 priority outlets
lead.headline: An arms offer to Xi, then a denial
lead.body:
Ambassador David Perdue told Fox News on Sep 27 that Trump had asked Xi Jinping at the White House summit whether China wanted to buy American weapons. The State Department said the next day that the US has no plans to sell weapons to China. Trump told reporters on Sep 28 he had "never heard of" such an offer, adding that Beijing would "probably like to buy it" but "we didn't discuss it." He later said Perdue "was probably talking about Taiwan," PBS reported.

Perdue also said US policy on Taiwan is unchanged after the visit. Taipei called its arms-sales dialogue with Washington "continuous" while a $14 billion package stays on hold.

research_roundup.headline: The Scope and Nature of the U.S.-China Competition
research_roundup.body: Michael J. Mazarr and colleagues open a multi-report RAND study with a plain finding: "The United States can protect its interests and gain leverage against China without blowing up the relationship."

research_roundup.headline: What did the Trump-Xi summit actually accomplish?
research_roundup.body: Ryan Hass, Yun Sun, Susan Thornton, Mireya Solís, Michael O'Hanlon and others on what the state visit reveals about where the relationship goes next.

research_roundup.tag: Asia Society Center for China Analysis · Sep 29
research_roundup.headline: What Actually Happened at the Xi-Trump Summit
research_roundup.body: A ChinaFile conversation with Neil Thomas, Lizzi C. Lee, Lyle Morris and others: the summit "launched the U.S.-China bilateral dialogue on artificial intelligence" and left Taiwan and technology competition unresolved.

research_roundup.headline: Trump Had the Chance to Address U.S.-China AI Safety. He Threw Xi a Party Instead.
research_roundup.body: Jeffrey Prescott on the gap between "sobering risk and opulent inaction" on AI safety.

research_roundup.headline: A Trump-Xi Summit Scorecard
research_roundup.body: Bonnie Glaser grades the visit item by item, starting from Trump's bet that the trappings of respect would advance his agenda with Beijing.

research_roundup.headline: Why Trump Rolled Out the Red Carpet for Xi, and Why He Shouldn't Have
research_roundup.body: Dan Blumenthal and Ian Jones argue the treatment tells allies "that they are irrelevant as Beijing and Washington manage world affairs as coequal powers."
